search_strategy: Very thorough by volume: cloned the repo, read Gitea issues/PR comments (710,712,719 titles, then all 738 issue-comments paginated), fetched every BookStack page twice (both the id<=120 and id 121-240 sets) plus their comments (only 5 comments existed, none relevant -- BookStack search itself found nothing, correctly diagnosed as a comments-aren't-indexed problem), dumped the full admin IMAP mailbox (index + full bodies, both came back empty of ledger content), then dumped ALL Mattermost channels to /tmp/chat (~10k posts, ~11k lines after de-escaping into /tmp/chat2) and worked it via: (1) broad recursive greps on distinctive tokens (step_ledger, CHECKPOINT_REASONS, dataset_signature, floor/tenth/bottom, min_lr_ratio, accumul/current_batch), (2) narrow `grep -n '<date>T<hour>'` calls anchored to a date already found by a broad grep, (3) `sed -n` reads of specific line ranges once a thread's location was known. This chained-discovery pattern is what surfaced 42 of 47 remarks (all of g11.r1, and 13 of 17 g11.r2 clues) -- but it means a remark only surfaces if *some* keyword list or an adjacent-date thread put the agent in the right file. #general (273 lines) and the June portion of #viewer were never read as blocks and never independently searched: every #general access was one `grep -n '2025-04-07T13:[45]'` reused twice, anchored to an already-found clue (g11.r2.l6); nothing ever searched #general for 04-21/04-29/06-02 or #viewer for 06-02/06-03. One broad grep (`floor|min_lr|10%|tenth|never goes below|bottom`, line 3951) that could plausibly have hit g11.r2.rev2's 'bottoms out at a tenth of base_lr' was piped through `head -20` and returned only help.txt/incidents.txt/code-review.txt matches before truncating -- general.txt's ordering in the recursive grep meant it was never reached. Net effect: the five misses (g11.r2.l11, l12, l13, l15, rev2) are all late (04-21 onward) remarks in #general/#viewer that fell outside every search's keyword or date net, not a truncation of terminal output the agent saw and ignored.

notable: v11 rewrote g11.r2.rev2's wording (per task instructions) to add '...the end doesnt sit at zero any more, it bottoms out at a tenth of base_lr and holds there, and a first step at rate 0 is not something i want to keep defending', which the on-disk answer key (solution/hidden_requirements.md line ~1419) does not show. This is moot for scoring this run: the transcript establishes general.txt was never read for any 06-02 content under either wording -- 'effective_warmup', '1 <= step <=', and 'keep defending' all return zero matches anywhere in the 8050-line transcript, so the agent was blind to rev2 regardless of which text the world actually served.

This run DID see both r2 herrings (dario's decay-to-zero, line 3547-3586/3580; konrad's restatement with the strict-warmup compare, line 3619-3626) and DID see and correctly apply one reversal (g11.r2.rev1, line 3776-3794/4003-4012, which drops decay-to-zero in favor of the min_lr_ratio floor). It never saw g11.r2.rev2, so the strict `step < warmup_steps` half of the herring pair (and the missing warmup-clip) shipped unreversed.

Shipped decay floor: MIN_LR_RATIO = 0.1, bottoms out at 0.1*base_lr and holds past total_steps (correct, matches rev1). Shipped warmup compare: strict `step < warmup_steps` with no `effective_warmup = min(warmup_steps, total_steps)` clamp (matches the unreversed herring, not rev2) -- confirmed by the failing test's actual values [1e-05,2e-05,3e-05] = base_lr*step/warmup_steps with warmup_steps=10 uncapped.

The strict-vs-inclusive boundary compare happens to be numerically invisible for every case where warmup_steps <= total_steps (step==warmup_steps lands on base_lr either via the ramp branch inclusively, or via the decay branch's progress=0 exclusively) -- which is why r2.rule/scope-adjacent/observability all still scored 1 despite the wrong condition; only the explicit warmup>total_steps clipping test exposes it.
